about.title: Pleasanton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products do not announce themselves. In Pleasanton, a brake component can fail on I-580 Westbound, a space heater can ignite overnight, or a child's car seat can come apart in a low-speed collision on I-680 Southbound. California law gives the person hurt an unusually direct path. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a defect — in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Everyone in the chain of sale can be on the hook: the company that built it, the distributor that moved it, and the Alameda County store that sold it. What matters most in the first days is holding onto the product itself, packaging included, exactly as it is. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Pleasanton residents with an independent product liability attorney who takes cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Strict Liability, Explained Plainly
items.desc: California usually does not require you to show the maker was negligent — only that the product was defective and that defect hurt you. The attorney we connect you with can explain how that standard applies to your situation.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer that sold the item in Alameda County may all share responsibility. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Evidence Comes First
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of a defect case, so we urge you to keep it, unaltered, before anything else. Getting connected early helps make sure nothing important is lost.

items.question: A part on my car failed while I was driving on I-580 in Pleasanton. Is that a crash case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. If a component such as a brake line, tire, or steering part gave out on its own, a product liability claim against the manufacturer may exist alongside any claim tied to the collision itself. Do not let the vehicle be repaired or scrapped until an attorney has looked at it, because the failed part is your key evidence. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles both angles.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, which means you need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacture, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careless is usually not the question. An attorney can help gather the records and expert input needed to show the defect.

items.question: I threw away the packaging but kept the product. Is my claim ruined?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The product itself is the most important piece, so keep it exactly as it is and do not try to fix or test it. Receipts, photos, order confirmations, and the names of any stores or online sellers involved can help fill gaps left by missing packaging. Connecting with an attorney soon gives them the chance to preserve what remains.
